paragraphs: An offline reinforcement learning agent can perform well while some of its internal components remain surprisingly weak. This paper investigates that mismatch through experiments examining three parts of an agent: its representations, value functions, and policy. Separating these components helps explain performance differences that an overall task score alone cannot reveal.

The experiments show that a better-performing agent can have relatively poor representations and inaccurate value estimates. This finding challenges the expectation that stronger overall behavior must reflect improvements throughout the learning system. The authors also show that their evaluation setups can identify bottlenecks, making the analysis useful for deciding which component needs attention.

Guided by these findings, the authors make a simple modification to IQL and report state-of-the-art performance. They additionally investigate when learned dynamics models help model-free offline agents, proposing uncertainty-based sample selection to reduce the effects of model noise. Together, the contributions connect component-level diagnosis with changes intended to improve the resulting agent.
neurips-2022-a-closer-look-at-offline-rl.tldr: Component-level experiments reveal surprising weaknesses in successful offline RL agents and motivate improvements to learning and model-generated sample selection.

paragraphs: Variational autoencoders learn internal representations and reconstruct inputs, but small visual changes can cause unexpectedly large changes in those outputs. This paper examines adversarial attacks designed to exploit that vulnerability. It considers several previously proposed attack objectives and develops a method to reduce their effect on the model's inference process.

The proposed defense uses Markov chain Monte Carlo during inference, with theoretical analysis motivating this choice. Placing the intervention at this stage means the method adds no training cost. The authors also report that performance on inputs without attacks does not decrease, so the stated benefit combines improved robustness with preserved ordinary-input performance.

The evaluation spans MNIST, Fashion MNIST, Color MNIST, and CelebA, together with beta-VAE, NVAE, and beta-TCVAE configurations. Across these tests, the method consistently improves robustness to adversarial attacks. The contribution is therefore an inference-stage approach supported across several datasets and VAE designs, with the stated aim of alleviating attacks rather than establishing complete immunity.
neurips-2022-alleviating-adversarial-att.tldr: An MCMC-based inference method improves VAE robustness to adversarial inputs without adding training costs or reducing reported clean-input performance.

paragraphs: Make-on-demand chemical libraries contain enormous numbers of compounds that can be synthesized, but their growth makes explicitly listing every possibility increasingly impractical. This paper introduces CSLVAE, a generative model designed to navigate these libraries. It represents the library as a differentiable hierarchy, allowing molecular generation to follow the library's underlying synthesis organization.

For an input compound, the encoder produces a retrieval query. The decoder then reconstructs the molecule by choosing its chemical reaction and subsequently its reactants. This design reduces sequential dependence in decoding and supports generation of large, valid molecular graphs. It also enables fast, parallel processing of batches from very large synthesis libraries.

Generated compounds are guaranteed to belong to the library, which the authors connect to synthetic and cost-effective accessibility. The model can also encode compounds outside the library and search for related compounds within it. Experiments demonstrate navigation of massive combinatorial libraries, supporting a way to explore accessible molecular candidates without explicitly enumerating the entire collection.
neurips-2022-an-efficient-graph-generati.tldr: CSLVAE navigates vast synthesis libraries by generating molecules through reaction and reactant choices that guarantee library membership.

paragraphs: A neural network can approximate a forward process, making it useful for searching backward from a desired result to a suitable input. The difficulty is that a solution must work in the original process, not merely in its learned approximation. Autoinverse addresses this distinction when inverting neural network surrogates for science and engineering.

Its central idea is to seek solutions near reliable examples sampled from the forward process and used to train the surrogate. During inversion, Autoinverse accounts for predictive uncertainty and minimizes it. This makes the surrogate's reliability part of the search itself, directing attention toward solutions supported by the data behind the approximation.

The authors describe the method as highly automated, initialization free, and equipped with embedded regularization and feasibility enforcement. They verify it on real-world problems in control, fabrication, and design. The stated contribution combines accurate inversion with explicit attention to whether proposed solutions remain useful when evaluated through the native forward process.
neurips-2022-autoinverse-uncertainty-awa.tldr: Autoinverse minimizes surrogate uncertainty during neural network inversion to seek feasible solutions near reliable training data.

paragraphs: Assessing a model's uncertainty requires a reliable way to measure the quality of its probabilistic predictions. This paper focuses on a problem with that measurement step: commonly used calibration-error estimators are often biased and inconsistent. Consequently, evaluating whether a recalibration method improves a model can itself involve an unreliable estimate.

The authors introduce proper calibration errors, a framework connecting calibration errors with proper scores. That relationship supplies a corresponding upper bound with optimal estimation properties. The upper bound matters because it provides a statistically supported route to quantifying calibration improvements, rather than relying entirely on the problematic estimators the paper examines.

The paper supports its argument with both theoretical and empirical comparisons showing shortcomings of commonly used estimators relative to the proposed approach. Because proper scores apply broadly, the framework also provides a natural extension of recalibration beyond classification. Its contribution is therefore both a better foundation for measuring improvement and a route to using that foundation in additional prediction settings.
neurips-2022-better-uncertainty-calibrat.tldr: Proper calibration errors connect calibration measurement to proper scores, yielding upper bounds that support reliable assessment beyond classification.

paragraphs: Teacher-student object detection often converts a teacher's final, sparse predictions into dense training supervision through hand-designed assignment rules. DTG-SSOD instead uses the teacher's dense information directly. The goal is to simplify this supervision pathway while preserving information that the conventional sparse pseudo-label representation leaves unused.

Two mechanisms implement the approach. Inverse NMS Clustering teaches the student to group candidate boxes according to the grouping information exposed by the teacher's non-maximum suppression procedure. Rank Matching then teaches the student to reproduce the teacher's ranking distribution within those groups. Together, these mechanisms transfer both relationships among candidates and their relative rankings.

The resulting method learns from unlabeled data without conventional sparse pseudo labels. On COCO, the authors report state-of-the-art performance across several labeling ratios. With 10% of the labels, it raises the supervised baseline from 26.9 to 35.9 mAP and exceeds Soft Teacher by 1.9 points. These results support dense teacher guidance as an effective source of supervision in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2022-dtg-ssod-dense-teacher-guid.tldr: DTG-SSOD improves semi-supervised detection by teaching students the teacher's candidate-box groupings and rankings directly.

paragraphs: Personalized federated learning aims to collaborate across clients while producing a model suited to each one. FedPop addresses two difficulties in this setting: quantifying uncertainty and personalizing models for new clients or clients with little data. These issues arise in both cross-silo and cross-device learning.

The method treats personalization as population modeling. Each client model combines common population parameters with random effects that represent differences among clients. This formulation puts shared structure and client variation into the same model, providing a basis for uncertainty quantification alongside personalized predictions. The authors develop federated stochastic optimization algorithms using Markov chain Monte Carlo to carry out the approach.

The paper provides nonasymptotic convergence guarantees for those algorithms and evaluates them on multiple personalized federated learning tasks. It reports robustness to client drift, practical inference for new clients, and uncertainty quantification with mild computational and memory overhead. The contribution brings these capabilities together within a population-based formulation rather than treating personalization and uncertainty as separate concerns.
neurips-2022-fedpop-a-bayesian-approach-.tldr: FedPop combines shared population parameters and client-specific random effects to support personalized federated learning with uncertainty quantification.

paragraphs: FlowHMM extends continuous hidden Markov modeling to observation distributions that need not follow Gaussian forms or Gaussian mixtures. The paper uses deep flow-based architectures to represent more complex densities while retaining hidden-state modeling. Its aim is to make the observation model adaptable to the shape and dimensionality of the data.

The authors propose two training strategies. One applies gradient-based learning directly to continuous multidimensional observations, but remains computationally expensive for longer sequences. The other works with a co-occurrence matrix built from discretized observations and models pairs of co-observed values. In that formulation, training time is independent of the training sequence length.

Experiments compare both strategies with Gaussian mixture baselines. The authors report improvements in recovering probability distributions, predicting hidden states, and assigning likelihood to unseen data. These findings support the value of more flexible observation densities across several evaluation criteria. The two training routes also address a practical choice between working directly with continuous sequences and learning from their discretized co-occurrence representation.
neurips-2022-flowhmm-flow-based-continuo.tldr: FlowHMM uses flow-based observation densities and two training strategies to improve continuous hidden Markov modeling beyond Gaussian mixtures.

paragraphs: Adversarial defenses commonly train against a specified set of attacks, but an attacker at deployment may have different or stronger capabilities. This paper formalizes that mismatch. It asks when robustness learned under a source threat model can generalize to an unknown, stronger target threat model.

The theoretical contribution is a generalization bound connecting the gap between the two threat models to variation in the feature extractor. Here, variation measures the expected maximum difference between extracted features across a threat model. This connection motivates variation regularization, which reduces feature variation under the source threat model during training.

Experiments show that variation regularization can improve generalization to unforeseen attacks. Combined with perceptual adversarial training, it achieves reported state-of-the-art robustness on those attacks. The significance is a link between a formal account of threat-model mismatch and a concrete training intervention. The empirical result supports improved transfer of robustness in the evaluated settings, while retaining the paper's qualified claim that such improvement can occur.
neurips-2022-formulating-robustness-agai.tldr: A bound relating threat-model generalization to feature variation motivates regularization that can improve robustness to unforeseen attacks.

paragraphs: Estimating the effects of a continuous treatment means learning how outcomes change across treatment levels, such as different doses. When treatment assignment is not randomized, differences among individuals can create selection bias and unreliable estimates. This paper develops theoretical support for reducing that bias when estimating an average dose-response function.

The authors combine reweighting with an Integral Probability Metric, or IPM, to bound counterfactual estimation loss. The IPM connects the observed factual domain with the infinitely many counterfactual domains associated with continuous treatment values. For practical implementation, they also provide a discretized approximation of this distance with a theoretical guarantee.

These results lead to ADMIT, which jointly learns a reweighting network and an inference network. The former aims to alleviate selection bias; the latter estimates factual and counterfactual outcomes. Synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments show ADMIT outperforming existing benchmarks. The work therefore connects a theoretical account of counterfactual error with a trainable method for improving dose-response estimation under the studied conditions.
neurips-2022-generalization-bounds-for-e.tldr: ADMIT combines reweighting and outcome estimation, guided by counterfactual-loss bounds for continuous treatment effects.

paragraphs: Policy Dissection aims to make an already trained reinforcement learning controller responsive to human input. Earlier approaches used goal-conditioned designs that required changes to rewards and training. This paper instead investigates how the controller's existing internal representation relates to the movement characteristics of the agent it controls.

Inspired by neuroscience studies of motor control, the authors develop a frequency-based method for aligning intermediate representations with kinematic attributes of behavior. They report that this alignment can turn a given learned policy into a human-controllable policy without modifying the neural controller or retraining it. The intervention uses information already present in the learned representation.

Evaluations include autonomous driving and locomotion. In unseen traffic scenes, the shared driving system substantially improves reported performance and safety. With human participation during inference, locomotion robots exhibit varied controllable motions despite having been trained only to move forward. These findings suggest that interpreting internal representations can provide a useful route to shared autonomy with existing reinforcement learning policies.
neurips-2022-human-ai-shared-control-via.tldr: Policy Dissection links learned controller representations to movement attributes, enabling human control without retraining the policy.

paragraphs: This paper studies how the latent samples supplied to a GAN affect the quality and diversity of its generated images. The authors observe that nearby latent samples produce nearby images through a continuous generator, yet those images can differ greatly in quality. Conversely, distant latent samples can produce similar or even identical images.

That second possibility connects latent sampling to mode collapse, where samples collectively map into a single mode. The proposed response is to insert an implicit transformation of the latent sample before it reaches the generator. Adversarial sample-mining techniques, including iterative fast gradient sign methods, construct these transformations from an initial latent distribution such as a Gaussian.

The authors also introduce GAN training pipelines that incorporate targeted latent transformations into the model's bilevel optimization. The intended benefit is to improve the learned mapping in both output quality and diversity. Experiments on visual data report improvements in both respects, supporting latent-space transformation as a useful intervention in the generation and training process.
neurips-2022-improving-generative-advers.tldr: Adversarially constructed latent transformations improve reported GAN image quality and diversity by changing the samples used for generation and training.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to infer directed interactions among agents from observations of their features over time. Its model, iSIDG, uses a variational approach to recover this structure in dynamical systems. A central concern is separating direct interactions from indirect relationships that can also appear in the observations.

The model repeatedly feeds its learned interactions back into the inference process. This feedback is intended to suppress indirect interactions and strengthen the representation of direction. Additional objective terms encourage smoothness, connectedness, and sparsity. The authors show that these terms promote more realistic structures and further reduce inferred indirect interactions.

Evaluation covers biological networks, simulated fMRI data, and physical simulations. The reported results show precise interaction inference and significant improvements over baseline models. The contribution combines iterative feedback with structural regularization, giving the model two complementary ways to refine the graph it learns. These findings support the approach across several kinds of dynamical-system data included in the evaluation.
neurips-2022-iterative-structural-infere.tldr: iSIDG iteratively refines directed interaction graphs and uses structural regularization to reduce indirect connections.

paragraphs: This paper considers object detection when only some classes have human-provided supervision. Objects from other classes must be discovered, grouped by visual similarity, and localized automatically. The task therefore extends beyond recognizing an existing label vocabulary: the detector must also organize and locate previously unlabeled categories.

The proposed RNCDL network first uses region proposals to locate candidate objects. It then learns to assign each region to either a known class or a newly discovered class. A long-tail constraint on these assignments reflects the unequal frequencies of classes in the real world. Training the detection network end to end connects localization with this broader classification objective.

On COCO and LVIS, the authors report substantially better results than multistage pipelines based on traditional clustering. They also apply the method to Visual Genome, where it learns to detect semantic classes without direct supervision for those classes. The findings support jointly learning discovery and detection under the stated assumption that supervision is available for some source classes.
neurips-2022-learning-to-discover-and-de.tldr: RNCDL learns to locate objects and discover novel categories while using supervision only for a subset of classes.

paragraphs: Probably approximately correct reinforcement learning asks an agent to identify a nearly optimal policy with a specified high probability. Although worst-case optimal algorithms exist, the number of samples required for a particular environment is less understood. This paper studies that question for deterministic episodic Markov decision processes with finite state and action spaces.

The authors establish upper and lower sample-complexity bounds that nearly match, leaving a squared-horizon factor and logarithmic terms. Both bounds use a new measure called the deterministic return gap, which describes suboptimality for state-action pairs. This gives the analysis a way to reflect the difficulty of an individual problem instance rather than only worst-case difficulty.

The lower bound is expressed as a linear program, but the proposed learning algorithms do not need to solve that program. Their design and analysis use minimum-flow concepts from graph theory and a new maximum-coverage exploration strategy. The result combines detailed instance-dependent guarantees with algorithms described as simple, within the paper's deterministic, finite, episodic setting.
neurips-2022-near-instance-optimal-pac-r.tldr: New instance-dependent bounds and simple exploration algorithms nearly characterize PAC learning complexity in finite deterministic episodic MDPs.

paragraphs: This paper formulates reinforcement learning decisions as an iterative process. An agent's behavior is defined by the steady-state distribution of a parameterized reasoning Markov chain. To select an action, the agent simulates that chain for enough steps to approach its steady state, and a new tractable policy-gradient estimate supports learning.

The framework separates the simplicity of each transition from the complexity of the eventual action distribution. The authors show that a simple Gaussian transition function can support approximation of any continuous action distribution. They also show that the number of reasoning steps needed for convergence can adapt to decision difficulty, and that reusing past solutions can accelerate the process.

The resulting algorithm achieves reported state-of-the-art performance on popular MuJoCo and DeepMind Control benchmarks, covering both proprioceptive and pixel-based tasks. These findings connect a flexible probabilistic formulation of action selection with strong empirical control results. The defining feature is that the policy's action distribution emerges through repeated reasoning transitions rather than a single direct distributional output.
neurips-2022-policy-gradient-with-serial.tldr: A learned reasoning Markov chain enables flexible action distributions and decision-dependent computation within policy-gradient reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Isotonic regression fits predictions subject to ordering constraints. This paper studies how to perform that fitting while providing differential privacy, including when the domain is a partially ordered set. For any Lipschitz loss, the authors give a pure-DP algorithm whose expected excess empirical risk scales roughly as the domain's width times the logarithm of its size, divided by the number of observations.

They also establish a lower bound that scales roughly as width plus logarithmic domain size, again divided by sample count. This lower bound applies even to approximate-DP algorithms. The bounds are near-matching, and the authors show that essentially better general bounds require using additional structure of the underlying partial order.

For totally ordered domains with absolute-error or squared-error losses, the algorithm admits a near-linear-time implementation. The paper also extends the approach to extra structural constraints on the fitted function. Together, these results address statistical accuracy, privacy, and computational efficiency, while distinguishing general partial orders from more structured cases.
neurips-2022-private-isotonic-regression.tldr: The paper gives private isotonic regression algorithms and near-matching error bounds, with near-linear implementations for selected totally ordered cases.

paragraphs: Reconstructing an image or volume can benefit from first fitting broad structure and then adding finer detail. Existing coordinate networks offer some control over represented frequencies, but are not readily suited to this coarse-to-fine optimization. This paper introduces an architecture and training scheme that provide finer control over which frequencies participate at each stage.

Two changes make the approach work. Skip connections preserve structure learned at one scale while the network fits finer-scale content. A new initialization scheme controls the model's frequency spectrum during successive optimization stages. Together, these changes support multiscale fitting, which matters in inverse problems where coarse-to-fine optimization helps avoid poor local minima.

The authors first demonstrate the method by fitting natural images from coarse to fine. They then evaluate single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction using synthetically generated datasets. The model learns high-resolution structures at multiple scales with results reported as comparable to the state of the art. The evidence connects architectural frequency control with practical multiscale reconstruction in these settings.
neurips-2022-residual-multiplicative-fil.tldr: Skip connections and frequency-controlled initialization enable coordinate networks to reconstruct images and volumes progressively from coarse to fine.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation depends on accurate predictions near object boundaries, where small spatial details help separate neighboring regions. Common convolutional operators can smooth those details, making boundary prediction harder. This paper addresses the issue at the operator level by transforming existing features into features that better preserve semantic boundary information.

The authors formulate boundary enhancement as anisotropic diffusion and introduce a learnable semantic diffusion network to approximate that process. The module combines a parameterized semantic difference convolution operator with feature fusion. Its mapping from backbone features to boundary-aware features is differentiable, allowing the enhancement process to be learned within the segmentation model.

SDN is designed as an efficient, flexible module that can be inserted into existing encoder-decoder architectures. Extensive experiments report consistent improvements over several typical state-of-the-art segmentation baselines on challenging public benchmarks. The findings support an approach in which improving how features represent boundaries can strengthen existing segmentation systems, without requiring the contribution to take the form of an entirely new segmentation architecture.
neurips-2022-semantic-diffusion-network-.tldr: SDN learns a diffusion-inspired feature transformation that improves boundary awareness in existing semantic segmentation models.

paragraphs: ShapeCrafter generates 3D shapes from descriptions that develop over several steps. The motivation is that people often begin with a broad description and add details after seeing an intermediate result. The model captures this process by conditioning a shape distribution on an initial phrase and updating that distribution as more phrases arrive.

Training such a system requires examples suited to recursive description, so the authors introduce Text2Shape++, containing 369,000 shape-text pairs. The model builds on vector-quantized deep implicit functions to represent local details used in refinements. This combination addresses both the data needed for sequential descriptions and the shape representation needed to express their details.

The reported results show shapes matching their descriptions and evolving gradually as additional phrases are supplied. The method also supports shape editing and extrapolation. These capabilities suggest applications in collaborative creative design, where a person can refine a description in response to the generated result. The central contribution is generation that accommodates an evolving description rather than requiring all details at once.
neurips-2022-shapecrafter-a-recursive-te.tldr: ShapeCrafter progressively updates a distribution of 3D shapes as users add descriptive phrases.

paragraphs: Neural combinatorial optimization can learn effective heuristics, but strong methods do not always make full use of the time available to solve a problem. This paper introduces simulation-guided beam search to give learned policies a stronger search procedure. The goal is to turn additional computation into better candidate solutions.

SGBS explores a tree while retaining a fixed-width set of candidates. Both a neural policy and simulation rollouts help identify promising possibilities. This combines learned guidance with examination of candidate continuations, allowing the search to investigate options beyond the initial output of the policy.

The authors also combine SGBS with efficient active search. The two methods reinforce each other: SGBS supplies better solutions for active-search updates, while active search improves the policy guiding SGBS. Evaluations on established combinatorial optimization benchmarks show significant solution-quality improvements under reasonable runtime assumptions. The contribution is thus a search mechanism, and a complementary learning loop, for using available solving time more effectively.
neurips-2022-simulation-guided-beam-sear.tldr: Simulation-guided beam search combines learned policies and rollouts to improve combinatorial solutions within practical runtime budgets.

paragraphs: This paper finds that neural networks can reveal useful uncertainty information through a simple change to their inputs. Networks starting from the same weights but trained on datasets shifted by constant biases produce slightly different predictions. The authors show that these differences strongly indicate epistemic uncertainty.

An analysis using the neural tangent kernel partly explains the effect: the kernel is not invariant to input shifts. Because the transformation is simple, the authors approximate the ensemble behavior with a single network. Their method, Delta-UQ, estimates predictive uncertainty by marginalizing over the effects of the biases during inference.

Evaluations cover outlier rejection, calibration under distribution shift, and sequential optimization of black-box functions. The authors report uncertainty estimates superior to many current methods across these benchmarks. The contribution links an observed sensitivity to data centering with a practical single-model uncertainty estimator, while the kernel analysis provides a partial explanation for why the underlying prediction differences carry useful information.
neurips-2022-single-model-uncertainty-es.tldr: Delta-UQ approximates uncertainty signals from bias-shifted training ensembles using a single neural network.

paragraphs: Image representations serve different needs: global features support classification, while local features are especially useful for detection and segmentation. VICRegL studies how to learn both kinds of features together without supervision. Its aim is to retain useful whole-image information while also learning detailed representations of image regions.

Two identical network branches receive differently distorted versions of the same image. The VICReg criterion trains pairs of global feature vectors and, simultaneously, pairs of local vectors from before the final pooling layer. Local pairs are pulled together when their feature distance is below a threshold or their positions agree with the known geometric transformation between views.

The authors report excellent detection and segmentation performance while maintaining good classification performance, with strong results on linear classification and segmentation transfer tasks. These findings address the trade-off between global and local learning objectives. The method shows that supervising both levels within the same self-supervised setup can produce representations useful across tasks with different spatial requirements.
neurips-2022-vicregl-self-supervised-lea.tldr: VICRegL jointly learns global and local image features to support classification, detection, and segmentation.

paragraphs: Generating convincing video requires both high-quality frames and consistency over time. This paper extends an image diffusion architecture to video and presents promising initial results toward that goal. The architecture supports joint training on images and videos, allowing both kinds of data to contribute to the same model.

The authors find that this joint training reduces minibatch-gradient variance and speeds optimization. They also introduce conditional sampling for extending videos in space and time, addressing the generation of longer and higher-resolution outputs. The proposed sampling technique performs better than previously proposed methods in the reported comparison.

The paper presents initial results on a large text-conditioned video generation task and reports state-of-the-art results on established video-prediction and unconditional-generation benchmarks. These findings cover both conditioning on available information and generating videos without such conditioning. The contribution combines an architectural extension, a useful joint-training strategy, and a sampling method for expanding outputs, while describing the broader progress in high-fidelity coherent video generation as promising.
neurips-2022-video-diffusion-models-6e55.tldr: A video diffusion architecture combines image-video training with conditional sampling for longer, higher-resolution generation.

paragraphs: Multi-view stereo uses multiple views to estimate scene depth, requiring both feature matching and aggregation of evidence across views. WT-MVSNet introduces window-based Transformers for these tasks. Its matching component uses epipolar constraints to reduce redundant comparisons while accounting for sensitivity to camera-pose and calibration errors.

Instead of restricting matching to points directly on epipolar lines, the Window-based Epipolar Transformer matches nearby windows. A shifted-window Transformer aggregates global information within the cost volume, and a Cost Transformer replaces 3D convolutions for cost-volume regularization. These components address correspondence search and the subsequent processing of matching evidence.

The method also adds a geometric consistency loss that penalizes unreliable regions where estimated depth maps disagree across views. This provides an additional constraint on the resulting depth predictions. The authors report state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets and first place on Tanks and Temples. The results support the combined use of geometric guidance, Transformer-based evidence processing, and consistency constraints in the evaluated reconstruction settings.
neurips-2022-wt-mvsnet-window-based-tran.tldr: WT-MVSNet combines geometry-guided window matching, Transformer cost processing, and multi-view consistency to improve depth reconstruction.
